units.title: A: Oral Communication Skills (Speaking + Listening Skills)

topics.title: Standard 1: Develop competence in listening and spoken language, to understand and communicate concrete information

outcomes.text: Recognize and repeat German sounds, words, basic phrases, and simple introductory questions.
Recognize familiar everyday German words and signs, and use common greetings and farewells.
Use familiar expressions and basic phrases to meet everyday communication needs.
Use numbers, prices, and dates in familiar everyday situations.
Recognize figures, prices, and times in announcements at places such as stations, airports, and shops.
Understand personal information and short conversations about nationality, family, routines, and hobbies.
Introduce yourself and ask and answer questions about residence, acquaintances, and possessions.
Extract essential information from short recordings or broadcasts about everyday matters.
Understand sequences of instructions for familiar activities such as sports, cooking, or booking.
Participate effectively in conversations with other people.

topics.title: Benchmark II: Communicate routine tasks requiring a simple and direct exchange of information on familiar and routine matters.

outcomes.text: Ask and give simple information about people and places using short, separate phrases.
Handle familiar routine tasks through simple, direct exchanges of information.
Follow the discussion topic and notice when it changes in clear, slow conversation; ask and answer personal questions.
Understand announcements about programs, events, and travel delays.
Show interest through simple language, gestures, and facial signals; communicate predictable information from signs, notices, posters, and programs.
Give brief, grammatically accurate answers with suitable pronunciation, using present, past, and future tenses to exchange information.
Produce brief phrases about personal details, likes, dislikes, and preferences.
Create dialogues, participate in role-play, and orally translate simple everyday words, signs, and phrases.
Recognize familiar words and signs shown with images, using known vocabulary, and distinguish between different sounds.
Recognize familiar names, words, and basic phrases in short, simple texts.
Explain unfamiliar words by using their surrounding context.
Infer unknown words or signs in familiar everyday texts and read familiar names, words, and phrases in short passages.
Answer short questions and multiple-choice items about brief illustrated stories.
Extract information from texts and present it through matching, linking, sequencing, or copying.
Understand and respond to short, simple texts containing everyday, work-related, or internationally shared vocabulary.
Understand and respond to texts containing everyday, job-related, or internationally shared vocabulary.
Find and understand essential information in advertisements, leaflets, and brochures.
Find specific information in lists, texts, leaflets, and notices, then respond appropriately.
Identify and read article, book, or chapter titles, captions, and subheadings.
Read simple stories and comics about familiar situations and understand main points in short reports or guides on everyday topics.
Use German salutations, greetings, and farewells appropriately.
Describe seasons and weather conditions.
Use vocabulary concerning the environment, weather, and seasons.
Discuss vocabulary related to weather.
Recognize and use the German alphabet.
Recognize and name food items.
Recognize and name common utensils.
Talk about food and drink in German.
Recognize and use restaurant food vocabulary, including menu, order, and bill.
Recognize and use names of traditional German dishes.
Give personal information such as name, address, and age.
Understand and use cardinal numbers.
Recognize and use the days of the week and months.
Tell the time using terms for hours, minutes, and seconds.
Discuss vocabulary associated with money.
Understand and use ordinal numbers.
Discuss city life and related activities.
Describe familiar places in a city, such as hospitals, railway stations, and restaurants.
Discuss different subjects and studies.
Use vocabulary for body parts, including hands, feet, and head.
Practise vocabulary related to health and the body.
Express emotions such as happiness, sadness, and tiredness.
Identify and use vocabulary for physical descriptions, including height and body size.
Accurately identify and pronounce country names and nationalities.
Discuss political life using appropriate German vocabulary.
Use German words for classroom objects and people, including teachers, students, furniture, and equipment.
Identify and recall basic colour names in German.
Describe common clothing items, including shirts, trousers, and shoes.
Discuss familiar topics such as home country, family, and school with suitable vocabulary.
Identify and discuss family members and relationships in German.
Identify and name common household furniture, including beds, chairs, tables, and sofas.
Enter conversations about familiar topics, give opinions, and exchange everyday information.
Use suitable vocabulary to manage everyday tasks and interactions in familiar situations.
Use suitable vocabulary to express basic communication needs.
Understand familiar words and expressions about oneself, family, school, hobbies, and surroundings when spoken slowly and clearly.
Use circumlocution and sufficient vocabulary to discuss everyday topics such as family, hobbies, work, travel, and current events.
Use a broad vocabulary for familiar topics and everyday situations.
Use varied simple vocabulary appropriately when discussing familiar subjects.
Read and understand short, simple texts containing frequently used vocabulary.
Write diary entries about activities, people, and places using basic vocabulary, simple sentences, and common connectives.
Write about personal impressions and opinions on interesting topics using basic everyday language.
Produce very short, understandable texts on familiar everyday subjects despite language errors.
Write simple information about personally relevant matters, including preferences, family, and pets.
Discuss different hobbies and sports activities in German.
Explain common means of transport, including buses, cars, and trains.
Identify and use travel vocabulary such as tickets, suitcases, and hotels.
Distinguish adjectives and apply their correct declensions.
Differentiate adjectives and adverbs and apply their correct declensions.
Identify animals and describe activities involving them.
State the German names of different occupations and professions.
Control elementary vocabulary well, while recognizing errors may occur with complex or unfamiliar subjects.
Recognize and use shopping vocabulary, including store, money, and price.
Describe everyday routines, including waking, washing, and going to bed.
Explain unfamiliar or multiple-meaning words using appropriate strategies.
Use sentence, paragraph, or text context to infer word and phrase meanings.
Use print or digital reference sources to check pronunciation, meaning, word class, or etymology.
Recognize and name vocabulary for nature and the environment, such as trees, flowers, and rivers.
Recognize and name vocabulary for nature and the environment, such as trees, flowers, and rivers.
Recognize and correctly apply word patterns showing changes in meaning or grammatical category.
Recognize and name German cultural celebrations, including Unity Day, Lantern Festival, Christmas, and Oktoberfest.
Recognize and use common everyday expressions, nouns, and adjectives.
Recognize and use German relative pronouns such as der, den, dem, die, das, dessen, and deren.
Understand and use the common irregular verbs sein and haben.
Form affirmative and negative sentences in the past tense using the Präteritum.
Identify and use nominative personal pronouns, including ich, du, wir, ihr, Sie, and sie.
Use conjunctions and infinitive constructions such as damit, um ... zu, wenn, dass, and zu.
Recognize and use definite articles der, die, and das, plus indefinite articles ein and eine.
Form sentences using verbs with their fixed prepositions.
Recognize conjugation rules for regular verbs such as kommen, kennen, and trinken.
Recognize and use indefinite determiners such as jeder, jede, jedes, and mehrere.
Construct and use irregular verbs such as fahren, schlafen, essen, and lesen.
Form nouns from verbs and adjectives through nominalisation.
Recognize and correctly use negation with nicht, kein, and keine.
Recognize and use the connectors denn, weil, and obwohl.
Apply the rules for correctly using German modal verbs.
Form sentences containing both dative and accusative objects.
Use direct and indirect objects together, including reflexive verbs with accusative and dative pronouns.
Use personal pronouns as direct objects in the accusative case.
Understand and use restrictive words such as nur, erst, and schon.
Recognize and conjugate separable verbs such as aufstehen, anrufen, ankommen, and abfahren.
Use frequency adverbs including meistens, oft, manchmal, ab und zu, selten, and nie.
Recognize and use place prepositions such as an, über, unter, vor, and neben.
Recognize and use place prepositions including zu, nach, umher, and gegenüber.
Use personal pronouns as indirect objects in the dative case.
Use personal pronouns as indirect objects in the dative case, including mir, dir, and ihm.
Recognize and use affirmative imperative sentences.
Form sentences using the present tense for future meaning and the recent past tense, Perfekt.
Recognize, pronounce, and use past-tense sentences in affirmative and negative forms.
Recognize and construct sentences containing reflexive verbs.
Use reflexive verbs with dative-case constructions.
Distinguish countable from uncountable nouns using indefinite pronouns such as wieviel, wieviele, einige, alle, and manche.
Use comparative and superlative forms with adjectives.
Use demonstrative pronouns such as diese and possessive adjectives such as mein, dein, and sein.
Use time prepositions such as von, bis, and ab correctly.
Form and use sentences in the passive voice.
Make polite requests and suggestions using Konjunktiv II.
Use phonetic sounds consistently to form words accurately.
Use a systematic strategy to check and correct word spelling.
Spell familiar and unfamiliar words correctly.
Apply rules for object genders and forming plurals from singular nouns in sentences.
Use punctuation marks correctly and understand their importance in sentences.
Write on varied topics accurately and fluently using correct grammar and organization.
Conjugate verbs and spell words correctly, applying umlauts and appropriate endings.
Conjugate verbs across tenses while maintaining accurate gender and number agreement.
Write simple phrases and complete forms with personal details such as name, age, nationality, and contact information.
Link simple phrases and sentences using connectors such as “und,” “aber,” and “denn.”
Write brief informal messages or letters to friends and family about holidays, celebrations, and activities.
Write simple formal or informal letters, including reports of problems connected with immediate needs.
Compose short messages or online posts stating preferences, likes, and dislikes in the present tense.
Write familiar texts such as diary entries, story introductions, and descriptions of events.
Use simple language to describe everyday objects, including their colour, size, and appearance.
Write about events, activities, and experiences using present and past tense information.
